newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BOTAFOGO RESERVES DENY FLAMENGO PLACE IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOTAFOGO RESERVES DENY FLAMENGO PLACE IN FINAL.

text.p: Flamengo, Brazil's best supported club, missed out on the final of the first stage of the Rio de Janeiro championship when they lost 1-0 on Wednesday to Botafogo, who controversially fielded their reserve team.
Botafogo, who had won all ten previous games, had already made sure of their place in next Sunday's final, which will now be against Vasco da Gama, and decided to rest their best players.
Flamengo had needed only a point from the match to edge out Vasco, who had bitterly criticised Botafogo's attitude with coach Antonio Lopes describing it as immoral.
But Flamengo, with striker Romario totally subdued, never got going and were stunned by a 25th minute goal from midfielder Renato, who was then sent off in the second half for a bad tackle.
Alejandro Mancuso, Flamengo's Argentine midfielder, was also shown the red card before halftime for punching an opponent.
Afterwards, Botafogo president Jose Luis Rolim hit out at the confusion of the tournament format.
"The only thing I regret is to have got Vasco into the final. The real disgrace is that we are eight points ahead of them but still have to fight for the title."
The rules of the competition have bemused players and fans alike.
The first of the three stages is decided by a play-off between the teams finishing first and second.
Yet the second and third stages do not have finals and will be won automatically by the team that finishes top. The winners of each of the three stages then take part in a play-off tournament.
The rules were changed after the contest had got under way because Flamengo, Fluminense and Botafogo did not like the original format and boycotted their opening matches.

"The competition began without the media and the supporters knowing the rules. It was only halfway through that we discovered there would be a game between the top two teams," said newspaper commentator Sergio Noronha.
"The directors of football in Rio have not yet noticed they are sinking in the same ship."
